accepted.s: Which geological formation occupies most of Andhra Pradesh and is associated with iron, manganese, copper, lead and gold?
accepted.x: Archaean rocks, including extensive gneiss, occupy most of Andhra Pradesh and contain iron, manganese, copper, lead and gold.
accepted.sec: Geological formations → minerals and region

accepted.s:
With reference to the Dharwar formation in Andhra Pradesh, consider the following statements:
1. It is associated with the Chittoor–Nellore region.
2. The Nellore schist belt is associated with mica.
3. It is mainly associated with coal deposits in the Godavari valley.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: The Dharwar formation occurs in the Chittoor–Nellore region and includes the Nellore mica schist belt. Coal in the Godavari valley is associated with the Gondwana formation.
accepted.sec: Geological formations → minerals and region

accepted.s: The Cuddapah formation of Andhra Pradesh is best described as which of the following?
o: A Cretaceous basaltic formation confined to small outliers
A Gondwana formation containing only coal deposits
A Proterozoic formation of about 1.6 billion years associated with barytes, limestone and uranium
A recent coastal formation containing only beach sands
accepted.x: The Cuddapah formation is Proterozoic, approximately 1.6 billion years old, and occurs mainly in the Kadapa, Nandyal, Kurnool, Annamayya and Prakasam areas. It contains barytes, limestone, uranium and other minerals.
accepted.sec: Geological formations → minerals and region

accepted.s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched?
o: Eastern Ghats khondalites — bauxite and graphite
Gondwana — coal in the Godavari valley
Deccan Trap — gold and lead deposits throughout the state
Kurnool system — sandstone, limestone and shale
accepted.x: The Deccan Trap consists of Cretaceous basalt and occurs only in small outliers. Gold and lead are associated mainly with Archaean rocks.
accepted.sec: Geological formations → minerals and region

accepted.s: The oldest geological basin of Andhra Pradesh is the:
accepted.x: The Kadapa or Cuddapah basin is regarded as the oldest basin of Andhra Pradesh.
accepted.sec: Geological formations → minerals and region

accepted.s:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:

List-I (Formation or belt)
a. Eastern Ghats mobile belt
b. Gondwana
c. Coastal sands
d. Kurnool Group

List-II (Principal association)
i. Coal
 ii. Bauxite, manganese and graphite
 iii. Ilmenite, rutile and zircon
 iv. Cement-grade limestone
accepted.x: The Eastern Ghats mobile belt contains bauxite, manganese and graphite; Gondwana contains coal; coastal sands contain ilmenite, rutile and zircon; and the Kurnool Group contains cement-grade limestone.
accepted.tq: Start from the sure formation–mineral pairs.
accepted.sec: Geological formations → minerals and region

accepted.s: Which of the following regions is associated with the Eastern Ghats khondalite formation in Andhra Pradesh?
o: Srikakulam to Nellore coastal belt only
accepted.x: The Eastern Ghats khondalite formation is associated with the Visakhapatnam Agency and contains bauxite, graphite and manganese.
accepted.sec: Geological formations → minerals and region

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Swarnagiri Gold Mine:
1. It was renamed from the Jonnagiri Gold Mine.
2. It is located in Tuggali mandal of Kurnool district.
3. It is associated with the Jonnagiri greenstone belt of the Eastern Dharwar Craton.
4. It is an underground mine operated under a ten-year lease.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Swarnagiri was renamed from Jonnagiri, lies in Tuggali mandal of Kurnool district and belongs to the Jonnagiri greenstone belt. It is an open-pit mine with a 30-year lease, so statement 4 is false.
accepted.tq: Reject the swapped mine-type and lease-duration statement.
accepted.sec: Gold - resource districts and private gold mine

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the Swarnagiri Gold Mine?
o: It is located in Gudur and produces mica as its principal mineral.
It is located in Ramagiri and operated by a public-sector company.
It is operated by APMDC under a five-year lease.
It is operated by GeoMysore Services under a 30-year lease.
accepted.x: The Swarnagiri mine is operated by GeoMysore Services under a 30-year lease and is located in Tuggali mandal of Kurnool district.
accepted.sec: Gold - resource districts and private gold mine

accepted.s: Commercial production from the Swarnagiri Gold Mine began in approximately:
accepted.x: Commercial production began in late June 2026. The mine is projected to produce about 1,000 kg of gold annually.
accepted.tq: Year-based factual recall with close distractors.
accepted.sec: Gold - resource districts and private gold mine

accepted.s: Ramagiri, in Anantapur district, is associated with which mineral resource?
accepted.x: Gold reserves occur at Ramagiri in Anantapur district, and gold-bearing quartz is found across parts of Rayalaseema.
accepted.sec: Gold - resource districts and private gold mine

accepted.s: The world's largest barytes deposit is located at:
o: Araku in Alluri Sitharama Raju district
accepted.x: Mangampeta in the YSR Kadapa district, within the Cuddapah basin, contains the world’s largest barytes deposit.
accepted.sec: Barytes - deposits and India/world share

accepted.s: Andhra Pradesh produces approximately what share of the world's barytes output?
accepted.x: Andhra Pradesh produces most of India’s barytes and nearly one-quarter of the world’s barytes output.
accepted.sec: Barytes - deposits and India/world share

accepted.s: The policy of Andhra Pradesh promotes beneficiation plants mainly for:
o: Low-grade iron ore and CDW-grade barytes
Beach sand minerals and coal only
accepted.x: The state policy promotes beneficiation plants for low-grade iron ore and CDW-grade barytes.
accepted.sec: Barytes - deposits and India/world share

accepted.s:
With reference to mica in Andhra Pradesh, consider the following statements:
1. The principal mica belt is the Gudur–Nellore belt.
2. Muscovite is white, phlogopite is amber and biotite is black.
3. Mica was declared a minor mineral in 2015.
4. Andhra Pradesh ranks second in India in mica production after Rajasthan.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. Rajasthan is stated to rank second in the relevant comparison, while Andhra Pradesh’s position is not second; hence statement 4 is false.
accepted.tq: Separate mineral varieties, legal status and rank.
accepted.sec: Mica belt - district, block mica, rank

accepted.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched?
accepted.x: Muscovite is white mica. Phlogopite is amber, biotite is black, and mica was declared a minor mineral in 2015.
accepted.sec: Mica belt - district, block mica, rank

accepted.s: The Jaipur–Udaipur mica belt is associated with which State?
accepted.x: Rajasthan has the Jaipur–Udaipur mica belt and ranks second in the stated comparison. Jharkhand includes the Koderma and Hazaribagh mica areas.
accepted.sec: Mica belt - district, block mica, rank

accepted.s: Tummalapalle uranium mine is located in:
o: Kurnool district, in the Kurnool Group
Srikakulam district, in the coastal sands
Nellore district, in the Dharwar belt
YSR Kadapa district, in the Cuddapah basin
accepted.x: Tummalapalle is located in YSR Kadapa district within the Cuddapah basin. The Indian uranium ore there is low-grade.
accepted.sec: Uranium and atomic minerals in beach sands

accepted.s: Which of the following pairs of uranium mines is located in Jharkhand?
accepted.x: Jaduguda and Narwapahar are uranium mines in Jharkhand. Tummalapalle is in YSR Kadapa district of Andhra Pradesh.
accepted.sec: Uranium and atomic minerals in beach sands

accepted.s: Thorium used in India’s nuclear programme is obtained mainly from:
accepted.x: Thorium is obtained from monazite and ilmenite beach sands. It is intended as fuel for Stage III of India’s three-stage nuclear programme and for the AHWR.
accepted.sec: Uranium and atomic minerals in beach sands

accepted.s: Which one of the following coastal sequences correctly represents the broad distribution of beach sands mentioned for Andhra Pradesh?
accepted.x: Coastal sands containing ilmenite, rutile, zircon, garnet and monazite extend broadly from Srikakulam to Nellore.
accepted.tq: Use the geographic range rather than a single deposit.
accepted.sec: Geological formations → minerals and region

accepted.s: Rare earth elements were reported in which rocks and district of Andhra Pradesh in 2023?
accepted.x: The National Geophysical Research Institute reported rare earth elements in syenite rocks of Anantapur district in 2023.
accepted.sec: Uranium and atomic minerals in beach sands

accepted.s: The statewide mineral-mapping initiative ordered by the Chief Minister is intended primarily to support:
o: Only the expansion of coal mining in the Godavari valley
Critical-mineral identification and value addition through APMDC
Replacement of all private mining leases by forest reserves
Exclusive export of unprocessed beach sand minerals
accepted.x: The initiative focuses on statewide mapping of critical minerals and value addition through APMDC. The identified focus minerals include titanium, lithium and gallium.
accepted.tq: Apply the stated policy objective to a practical scenario.
accepted.sec: Uranium and atomic minerals in beach sands

accepted.s: Which group contains the critical minerals specifically mentioned as current focus minerals in Andhra Pradesh’s mineral-mapping initiative?
accepted.x: The current focus minerals specifically mentioned are titanium, lithium and gallium.
accepted.sec: Uranium and atomic minerals in beach sands

accepted.s:
Arrange the following mineral deposits of Andhra Pradesh from the district associated with barytes to the district associated with uranium and then to the district associated with gold:
A. Jonnagiri
B. Mangampeta
C. Tummalapalle
accepted.x: Mangampeta is the barytes deposit in YSR Kadapa, Tummalapalle is the uranium mine in YSR Kadapa, and Jonnagiri is the gold mine in Kurnool. Thus the sequence is B, C, A.
accepted.tq: Order the listed sites by the mineral specified in the stem.
accepted.sec: Gold - resource districts and private gold mine
